text:
maya: Heads up — after the kernel 6.1 rollout to westus3 GPU pool I'm seeing a rapid conntrack surge and pod connections being dropped, a few model-serving pods restarted automatically. Anyone else seeing this?

santiago: yep, saw retries in the model-prefetch service. lots of `SYN_RECV`/`UNREPLIED` entries. opening a runbook and paging infra-oncall.

dylan: capturing packets now. quick check: `iperf3 -c 10.0.3.22 -M 9000` fails from some nodes, works from others. suspect MTU mismatch after driver + kernel change.

julia: checked node metrics: conntrack_count jumped from ~60k to 980k in ~7m on gpu-pool-westus3-az2 nodes. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` shows high values. `conntrack -S` shows spikes in new tcp flows.

maya: logs from a restarted pod show `connect: connection reset by peer` and many GOVEC warnings. Could the kernel's RDMA offload behavior have toggled GRO/GSO? I remember the 6.x kernel changed some offload defaults.

santiago: plausible. also seeing lots of outbound SNAT on node IPs — ephemeral port attrition. `ss -s` shows large TIME_WAIT and many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.

julia: we temporarily bumped `nf_conntrack_max` to 1_200_000 on a few nodes to avoid immediate drops: `echo 1200000 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`. that buys time but memory usage spiked.

dylan: note: increasing conntrack_max is risky — kernel allocates memory; if we go too far we risk OOM and kubelet churn. alternative short-term mitigations: reduce `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`, enable node-local egress to avoid SNAT for internal egress, and disable iptable conntrack helper for known flows.

maya: can we change timeouts safely? what to set?

santiago: propose `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait=30` on impacted nodes, plus add a watch to revert after the kernel rollback.

dylan: running that now on az2 nodes. also toggling `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` on a test node to see if it reduces conntrack creation rate (will report in 2m).

julia: infra dashboard: created a per-node conntrack alert for >70% and a dashboard panel for `ephemeral_port_usage` and `pod_reconnects`. opened INC-4579 and linked logs.

maya: cost/ops note: if we punt to cloud NAT scaling it's expensive — rough estimate +$3.5k/day if we flip to extra NAT capacity for westus3 egress. prefer local mitigations if possible.

santiago: agreed. short plan: 1) apply timeout tweaks cluster-wide for westus3, 2) roll back kernel on affected AZ (we can do targeted rollback on az2 where spike is worst), 3) pin high-throughput model-prefetch pods to older nodes (taint/toleration) until next validated kernel, 4) investigate RDMA driver offload flags and MTU negotiation.

dylan: test results: toggling GSO/GRO reduced conntrack creation on the test node by ~40% in 5m window, and `iperf3` with 1500 MTU succeeded from those nodes. looks like jumbo negotiation failed and kernel was fragmenting traffic, creating many short-lived flows.

julia: assigning tasks in INC-4579: @santiago — kernel rollback plan + smoke tests; @dylan — produce a short frag/mtu checklist and a probe to detect mismatch automatically; @maya — coordinate pinning and service rollouts + communicate to customers if we need a broader rollback.

infra-oncall-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled rollback job for nodes gpu-pool-westus3-az2-0..3 at 2026-03-18T12:20:00Z (per incident INC-4579).

maya: temporary mitigations applied: timeouts tweaked and prefetch pods pinned. early signals look better but still monitoring. will follow up when rollback completes.

santiago: timeline note — if rollback doesn't reduce conntrack by 80% in 30m we'll consider IP egress isolation by per-pod NAT or temporary nat-gateway scale.

dylan: adding a one-off conntrack sweeper: `conntrack -D --state INVALID,UNTRACKED` and a gentle cron to prune UNREPLIED after verifying side effects. use with caution.

julia: +1 on pruning but log all deletions. also capturing `dmesg | grep -i conntrack` and NIC driver messages for postmortem.

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread as the single source. will post final RCA and cost breakdown after wrap. :thumbsup:
